nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in FIG4 impair the polyphosphoinositide 5-phosphatase it encodes. FIG4 is a catalytic subunit of the PI(3,5)P2 biosynthetic complex (with the kinase PIKFYVE and the scaffold VAC14). Loss of FIG4 removes both its catalytic activity and a non-catalytic, complex-stabilizing role, and because FIG4 is also required for normal PIKFYVE activity, its loss reduces rather than raises PI(3,5)P2. A catalytically inactive FIG4 transgene still prevents the early vacuolization and neurodegeneration, indicating that much of the early defect reflects loss of the structural role rather than catalysis.

nodes.description: Disrupted endolysosomal homeostasis during corticogenesis produces an abnormal, excessively folded cortex (polymicrogyria). In the originally reported family the malformation was temporo-occipital (see the note on the MONDO/OMIM label below).

evidence.reference_title: Role of the phosphoinositide phosphatase FIG4 gene in familial epilepsy with polymicrogyria.
evidence.snippet: Histologic examination of Fig4-null mouse brain revealed neurodevelopmental impairment in the hippocampus, cortex, and cerebellum as well as impaired cerebellar gyration/foliation reminiscent of human cortical malformations.

nodes.description: Loss of FIG4 function reduces the abundance of phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate, a low-abundance signaling lipid on the cytoplasmic surface of endolysosomal membranes to which neurons are especially sensitive.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic Mutations of VAC14 in Pediatric-Onset Neurological Disease.
evidence.snippet: PI(3,5)P2 is a low-abundance signaling lipid that is localized to the cytoplasmic surface of endolysosomal vesicles.

nodes.description: Polymicrogyria is the defining cortical malformation. The originally reported family (PMID:24598713) had a temporo-occipital distribution; the MONDO/OMIM concept names a bilateral parasagittal parieto-occipital distribution (see entry notes).
